paragraphs.title: The Promise to Restore the Mountains and the Land of Israel

answers: The mountains of Israel
The kings of the heathen
The people of Egypt
easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Ezekiel to speak to the mountains of Israel.
easy.q: To whom was Ezekiel commanded to prophesy at the beginning of the passage?

answers: They would be holy forever
They were theirs in possession
They would remain empty
easy.explanation: The enemy said, “The ancient high places are ours in possession.”
easy.q: What did the enemy say about the ancient high places?

answers: Branches and fruit
Gold and silver
Weapons and shields
easy.explanation: The Lord promised, “Ye shall shoot forth your branches, and yield your fruit to my people of Israel.”
easy.q: What would the mountains of Israel give to the people of Israel?

answers: Because the land was too fertile
Because they had borne the shame of Israel
Because Israel had built no cities
medium.explanation: The Lord said that Israel had borne the shame of the heathen, and He spoke in jealousy and fury.
medium.q: Why did the Lord speak against the heathen in the fire of His jealousy?

answers: A land or property claimed as one’s own
A place of prayer
A fortified city
medium.explanation: The enemy claimed the mountains and land as its own possession.
medium.q: What does “possession” mean in the enemy’s statement about the land?

answers: Exile, famine, and destruction
Fruitfulness, settlement, increase, and security
War, conquest, and punishment
medium.explanation: The Lord promised cultivation, sowing, inhabited cities, multiplied people and beasts, and peace.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the restoration of the land?

answers: The enemy claimed the land, but the Lord promised to restore it to Israel
The enemy wanted to build the cities, but the Lord promised to destroy them
The enemy wanted to make the land fruitful, but the Lord promised to leave it desolate
challenge.explanation: The enemy claimed the land as its possession, while the Lord promised its restoration for Israel.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the enemy’s words and the Lord’s promise?

answers: The land would no longer be regarded as causing the loss of its inhabitants
The land would no longer need cultivation
The heathen would never enter the land again
challenge.explanation: The Lord promised that the land would no longer be blamed for devouring or bereaving its people.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the promise that the land would no longer bereave them of men?

answers: The restored land would show that the Lord had acted for it
The fruitfulness would keep the people from learning God’s statutes
The fruitfulness would cause the heathen to rule the land
challenge.explanation: The Lord connects the land’s restoration with the people knowing that He is the Lord.
challenge.q: How are the fruitfulness of the land and the knowledge of the Lord connected?

paragraphs.title: Israel’s Sin and the Profanation of God’s Name in Exile

answers: By their way and their doings
By building cities
By sowing fields
easy.explanation: The passage says that Israel defiled the land by their own way and doings.
easy.q: How had the house of Israel defiled the land?

answers: He multiplied their fruit
He scattered them among the heathen
He settled them in the cities
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries.”
easy.q: What did the Lord do because of their ways and doings?

answers: The holy name of the Lord
The borders of Egypt
The mountains of the heathen
easy.explanation: Israel profaned the Lord’s holy name when they were scattered among the nations.
easy.q: What did Israel profane among the heathen?

answers: Bloodshed and idols
Building cities and working fields
Gathering Israel and keeping the statutes
medium.explanation: The passage refers to the blood Israel had shed and the idols with which they had polluted the land.
medium.q: What were among the acts that defiled the land?

answers: A way of life regarded as unclean before the Lord
A way of rejoicing and feasting
A way of returning to the land
medium.explanation: The comparison describes the uncleanness of Israel’s way before the Lord.
medium.q: What does “the uncleanness of a removed woman” describe in this passage?

answers: To sanctify His great name among the heathen
To punish the mountains of Israel
To give the land to the heathen
medium.explanation: The Lord emphasized that He acted for His holy name’s sake, which Israel had profaned.
medium.q: Why did the Lord say that He was not doing these things for Israel’s sake?

answers: The heathen thought Israel’s departure from the land dishonored Israel’s God
The exile caused the heathen to leave their own lands
The exile kept the heathen from knowing about Israel
challenge.explanation: The heathen saw that Israel, called the people of the Lord, had gone out of His land, and this profaned His name.
challenge.q: What was the connection between Israel’s exile and the profanation of the Lord’s name?

answers: Sanctifying His great name before their eyes
Scattering Israel through the countries
Leaving the land desolate
challenge.explanation: The Lord said the heathen would know that He is the Lord when His name was sanctified in Israel before their eyes.
challenge.q: Which action was directly intended to make the heathen know who the Lord is?

answers: The restoration was not presented as a reward for Israel’s works
Israel had no connection with the restoration
The Lord would not bring Israel back to the land
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that the central purpose was the sanctifying of the Lord’s name, not Israel’s merit.
challenge.q: What does the repeated statement that the Lord was not acting for Israel’s sake emphasize?

answers: Out of all countries
Only from Jerusalem
Only from the mountains of Seir
easy.explanation: The Lord promised to gather Israel out of all countries and bring them into their own land.
easy.q: From where would the Lord gather the children of Israel?

answers: Clean water
The fire of war
The fruit of the land
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean.”
easy.q: With what would the Lord cleanse Israel?

answers: An heart of flesh
An heart of gold
An heart of fire
easy.explanation: The Lord promised to take away the stony heart and give Israel an heart of flesh.
easy.q: What would the Lord give Israel instead of a stony heart?

answers: Gathering, cleansing, a new heart, and God’s Spirit
War, exile, famine, and rebuilding
Increase, conquest, destruction, and exile
medium.explanation: The Lord would gather Israel, cleanse them, give them a new heart and spirit, and cause them to obey His statutes.
medium.q: What is the main order of changes described in the passage?

answers: An inward condition resistant to spiritual change
A physically strong heart
A heart belonging to a stranger
medium.explanation: The stony heart represents Israel’s former unresponsive spiritual condition.
medium.q: What does “a stony heart” represent in this passage?

answers: They would walk in His statutes and keep His judgments
They would leave the land
They would forget their former ways
medium.explanation: The Lord promised to cause them to walk in His statutes and keep His judgments.
medium.q: What would result from the Lord putting His Spirit within Israel?

answers: Cleansing from uncleanness is joined with a changed heart and spirit
Cleansing removes the need for inner transformation
Inner transformation occurs only after Israel leaves the land
challenge.explanation: The Lord promises both cleansing from uncleanness and the replacement of the stony heart with a new heart and spirit.
challenge.q: How are cleansing and inner transformation related in the passage?

answers: They would loathe themselves and be ashamed of their iniquities
They would return to those same ways
They would teach the heathen the ways of sin
challenge.explanation: Their remembrance would lead them to loathe themselves and be ashamed and confounded for their sins.
challenge.q: Why would Israel remember their evil ways and doings?

answers: It describes the renewal of the relationship between the Lord and Israel
It announces the end of the relationship between the Lord and Israel
It transfers the land to the heathen
challenge.explanation: The words describe the restored covenant relationship between Israel and the Lord.
challenge.q: What does the connection between “ye shall be my people” and “I will be your God” teach?

paragraphs.title: Rebuilding the Cities and Reviving the Land

answers: He would rebuild them
He would sell them
He would abandon them
easy.explanation: The Lord said that the cities would be inhabited and the wastes would be builded.
easy.q: What would the Lord do to the ruined cities?

answers: It would be tilled
It would remain desolate
It would be covered with water
easy.explanation: The desolate land would be tilled where it had lain desolate.
easy.q: What would happen to the desolate land?

answers: The garden of Eden
A closed desert
A battlefield
easy.explanation: The heathen would say, “This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden.”
easy.q: What would the land become like after its restoration?

answers: The cities would be inhabited and the wastes built
Israel would be scattered again
The land would remain desolate
medium.explanation: In the day of cleansing, the Lord would cause Israel to dwell in the cities and rebuild the wastes.
medium.q: What would follow the cleansing of Israel?

answers: Empty and lacking inhabitants or cultivation
Fertile and full of harvest
Holy and filled with pilgrims
medium.explanation: The desolate land was empty and unused, but the Lord promised that it would be tilled.
medium.q: What does “desolate” mean in the phrase “the desolate land”?

answers: The heathen who remained round about Israel
Only the people of one central city
Only the prophet
medium.explanation: The heathen left round about Israel would know that the Lord had rebuilt and planted the land.
medium.q: Who would know that the Lord had built the ruined places and planted the desolate land?

answers: The cities are rebuilt and the land is cultivated before the eyes of observers
Only the hearts of the people change while the land remains unchanged
The restoration happens secretly without witnesses
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes rebuilt cities, cultivated land, passersby, and the surrounding heathen who would see the change.
challenge.q: What makes the restoration a visible testimony rather than only an inward change?

answers: It changes from desolation and ruins to cultivation and inhabited cities
It changes from fruitful land to desolation
It changes from inhabited cities to an empty wilderness
challenge.explanation: The land moves from desolation, waste, and ruined cities to cultivation, rebuilding, and habitation.
challenge.q: What is the contrast between the land’s condition at the beginning and at the end of the passage?

answers: The Lord’s promise will be carried out in action, not left as words
The prophet cancels the promise
The heathen will rebuild the land without the Lord
challenge.explanation: The ending stresses both the Lord’s authority to promise and His power to fulfill the restoration.
challenge.q: What does the ending “I the Lord have spoken it, and I will do it” mean?

paragraphs.title: The Multiplication of People in the Ruined Cities

answers: Like a flock
Like trees
Like the stars
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I will increase them with men like a flock.”
easy.q: Like what would the Lord multiply the house of Israel?

answers: Flocks of men
Water
Weapons of war
easy.explanation: The waste cities would be filled with “flocks of men,” meaning many people.
easy.q: What would fill the waste cities?

answers: The holy flock and the flock of Jerusalem in her solemn feasts
An army going to battle
Fruit growing in a field
easy.explanation: The passage compares the multiplication to the holy flock and the flock of Jerusalem during its solemn feasts.
easy.q: To what was the increase of people compared?

answers: The increase would fill the cities that had been waste
The increase would cause the cities to be destroyed
The increase would occur only outside the land
medium.explanation: The passage says that the waste cities would be filled with flocks of men.
medium.q: What is the connection between the increase of people and the waste cities?

answers: Flocks associated with the sacred gatherings and solemn feasts
Sheep that belonged to no one
Sheep found in the wilderness
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the flocks brought to Jerusalem in connection with its solemn feasts.
medium.q: What does “the holy flock” refer to in this context?

answers: They would know that the Lord is God
The land would remain uninhabited
The heathen would forget Israel
medium.explanation: The verse concludes that through this increase they would know that the Lord is God.
medium.q: What would be the result of filling the cities with people?

answers: It emphasizes a great and orderly gathering in a sacred setting
It shows that the cities would remain empty
It shows that Israel would return only to farming
challenge.explanation: The comparison highlights the great multitude gathered in Jerusalem during sacred festival times.
challenge.q: Why is the comparison to Jerusalem’s flock at the solemn feasts appropriate?

answers: The rebuilt cities are completed by being filled with people
The restoration ends with the land remaining desolate
The restoration consists only of changing the stony heart
challenge.explanation: After the land and cities are rebuilt, the return and multiplication of people complete the visible restoration.
challenge.q: How does the final passage complete the restoration of the land?

answers: The increase is a visible sign of the Lord’s work and leads to recognition of Him
The increase prevents the heathen from seeing the Lord’s work
The increase proves that Israel acted without the Lord’s help
challenge.explanation: The multiplication, like the restoration of the land, is presented as an act through which people know that the Lord is God.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the multiplication of people and knowing the Lord?
